official.deadline_central_display: October 19-23, 2026, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time, depending on Major Field of Study (Life Sciences Oct 19; CISE, Materials Research, Psychology, Social Sciences Oct 20; Engineering Oct 22; Chemistry, Geosciences, Mathematical Sciences, Physics and Astronomy Oct 23)
official.deadline_note: Reference letters are due earlier, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 16, 2026. Application deadlines vary by Major Field of Study between October 19 and October 23, 2026, and all applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date. official.status_note: The solicitation NSF 26-526 is live with deadlines in October 2026; NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring, and support of new fellowships is pending availability of funds.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For each of the three years of support, NSF provides a $16,000 Cost of Education allowance provided to the institution of higher education in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a Fellowship year.
benefits: Three years of support over a five-year Fellowship period
$37,000 stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of support
$16,000 Cost of Education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees
The Fellowship is portable and can be transferred to a different institution of higher education after completion of the first Fellowship year
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or permanent resident (green-card holder)
Must intend to enroll, or be enrolled, full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM
Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program at the time of application (non-degree coursework clearly identified on the transcript does not count)
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship, and must have declined any previously offered Fellowship by the deadline

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
Must not be a current NSF employee; an eligible applicant may submit only one application per annual competition
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan, as it determines the application deadline and reviewers
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
Request and rank reference letters; three reference writer names and contact information are required and two letters must be received by NSF
Applications are automatically checked by the module for format compliance; non-compliant documents are not accepted
documents: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (maximum three pages, PDF)
Graduate Research Plan Statement (maximum two pages, PDF)
Official undergraduate academic transcripts (PDF format), and graduate transcripts if applicable
Two reference letters, plus three reference writer names and contact information
Completed application package submitted in the GRFP Application Module
selection_criteria: Two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society)

Intellectual Merit factors include ability to plan and conduct research, work independently and in a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems and persist through challenges

Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, and developing a globally competitive STEM workforce
coverage: $37,000 stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of support
$16,000 Cost of Education allowance provided to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each fellow using the support in a fellowship year
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community, and supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave
application_method: Create a Research.gov account and access the GRFP Application Module (which usually opens in July or August)
Enter personal information, education and experience, select the Major Field of Study, upload transcripts and statements, and submit by the deadline for that field
official.application_route: One application per annual competition through the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov, with a field-specific October deadline and reference letters due October 16, 2026.
official.study_mode: Full-time research-based master's or doctoral degree programs
official.citizenship_residency: U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international applicants except permanent residents of the United States
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: NSF-supported STEM fields; practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) and joint science-professional degree programs are excluded
official.research_requirement: A Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings is required
official.duration: Five-year Fellowship period with three years of financial support
official.description: The NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students pursuing full-time research-based master's and doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM disciplines at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period - a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees - with no post-graduate service requirement, and an estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation pending availability of funds.
official.program_type: Government fellowship (NSF Division of Graduate Education)

applicant_utility.summary: The GRFP clock is field-specific: your Major Field of Study fixes your deadline anywhere from October 19 to 23, 2026, and reference letters are due even earlier on October 16 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern - request letters in September, not October. The application is capped at three pages for the personal statement and two for the research plan, both requiring explicit Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings, and Research.gov auto-rejects non-compliant formats, so convert everything to PDF and check page counts before uploading. Citizenship is a hard gate (US citizen, national or permanent resident), and you must have completed less than one academic year of graduate study, so this is fundamentally a senior-undergraduate and first-year-graduate award - later-stage students are simply ineligible.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates, bachelor's holders with no prior graduate enrollment, and first-year research-based STEM graduate students who are US citizens, nationals or permanent residents.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm citizenship or permanent-resident status and that you have completed less than one academic year in a graduate program
Pick your Major Field of Study deliberately - it determines both your deadline and your reviewer panel
Request reference letters in September so at least two arrive by 8:00 p.m. ET on October 16, 2026
Draft the statements to exact limits (three pages personal, two pages research plan) with the required Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts headings
Upload transcripts as PDF and submit early enough that the module's automatic format check passes on the first attempt
common_rejection_risks: Missing the field-specific October deadline or the reference-letter cutoff - no extensions are granted
Exceeding the three-page or two-page statement limits, or lacking the mandated section headings
Selecting a Major Field misaligned with the proposed research, sending the application to the wrong reviewers
Applying after completing a full academic year of graduate study, or having previously accepted a Fellowship
Targeting a professional program (MBA, MD, JD, MPH, MSW and similar), which is excluded at any time during the fellowship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The fellowship covers tuition and mandatory fees via the $16,000 cost-of-education allowance plus a $37,000 stipend, but fellows must plan for the two unfunded years within the five-year fellowship period.
document_audit: Reference writers receive email instructions through the module - give them weeks of notice and confirm they have received the request
Non-degree coursework must be clearly identified on the transcript so it does not count against the one-year graduate study limit
All materials go through the GRFP Application Module; emailed or mailed applications are not accepted
alerts: One application per annual competition - a second submission voids your attempt
The fellowship is portable only after the first fellowship year; funds flow through the institution, which disburses the stipend to you
Withdrawal before November 15, 2026 keeps the application from counting against your allowed number of attempts
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Research.gov account, GRFP Application Module entries and uploads, references landing by October 16, 2026, and final submission by your field's October 19-23 deadline at 8:00 p.m. Eastern; NSF notifies in spring.

benefits: Africa: up to 3-year Fellowship of US $15K to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel
Australia and New Zealand: 1-year Fellowship of AUD $20K to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel

Canada and the United States: up to 2-year Fellowship of US $85K per year towards education costs (tuition and fees), living expenses, travel, and personal equipment (effective from 2025 for new recipients)

Europe and the Middle East: up to 2-year Fellowship with a yearly bursary towards stipend or salary, health care, social benefits, tuition and fees, conference travel and personal computing equipment, varying by country

India: up to 4-year Fellowship of US $50K for early-stage PhD students, or a 1-year Fellowship of US $10K for late-stage PhD students; Latin America: up to 2-year Fellowship of US $15K per year; Southeast Asia: up to 3 years of US $10K per year or up to graduation, whichever is earlier; East Asia: 1-year Fellowship of US $10K
eligibility: Enrolled full-time in a PhD program in computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees to PhD students
Must be nominated by an eligible university during the application window; direct applications from students are not accepted
Must remain enrolled full-time in the PhD program for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award
Google employees, and their spouses, children and members of their household, are not eligible
Students already supported by a comparable industry award are not eligible; government or non-profit organization funding is exempt
Past awardees from the PhD Fellowship program are not eligible to apply again

Region-specific stage requirements: Canada and the United States require completed graduate coursework by the academic award year; East Asia requires most graduate coursework completed; Africa, India, Latin America and Southeast Asia allow incoming or early-stage students; Europe and the Middle East allows any stage
requirements: Be nominated by an eligible university during the application period
Submit all materials in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file
Include a research or dissertation proposal of maximum 3 pages excluding references
Meet the region-specific student stage requirement
documents: Student CV with links to website and publications, if available
Research or dissertation proposal (maximum 3 pages, excluding references)
Transcripts of current and previous academic records
Two to three letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work, at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students
Cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming eligibility (Africa, Europe, Middle East, Canada, East Asia, United States, Latin America) and a one-page CV of the primary PhD advisor
Region-specific student essay responses of up to 350 words each for Canada, East Asia, the United States and Latin America
selection_criteria: Strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements and leadership potential
Proposals are evaluated for innovative concepts relevant to Google's research areas, robustness and potential impact, and should align with Google AI Principles
In Canada, the United States, East Asia and Latin America, essay responses are evaluated in addition to application materials

Universities may nominate up to four students in Canada and the United States, up to three in Africa, Australia, New Zealand, East Asia, Europe, India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, and any number in Latin America
coverage: Region-specific monetary awards covering combinations of stipend, tuition and fees, living expenses, travel and personal equipment as published per region
Awards are paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution with no overhead assessed against them
application_method: Contact your department or graduate school about the university's internal nomination process
If nominated, the university submits the application on your behalf through the portal, which becomes available on the program page when the application period begins
official.application_route: Students cannot apply directly - your university must nominate you during the application window and submit a single flat PDF on your behalf.
official.study_mode: Full-time PhD enrollment for the duration of the Fellowship
official.citizenship_residency: No general citizenship restriction; region lists are Africa, Australia, Canada, East Asia, Europe, India, Latin America, the Middle East, New Zealand, Southeast Asia and the United States
official.international_eligibility: Open to PhD students worldwide in the listed regions, subject to university nomination
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees; research areas include machine learning, machine perception, NLP, HCI, quantum computing, privacy, systems, algorithms and health research
official.research_requirement: Research or dissertation proposal of maximum 3 pages excluding references, aligned with Google's published research areas and Google AI Principles
official.duration: One to four years depending on region: Africa up to 3 years, Australia and New Zealand 1 year, Canada and the United States up to 2 years, East Asia 1 year, Europe and the Middle East up to 2 years, India up to 4 years (early-stage) or 1 year (late-stage), Latin America up to 2 years, Southeast Asia up to 3 years
official.description: Google PhD Fellowships directly support graduate students as they pursue their PhD, recognizing outstanding students doing exceptional and innovative research in areas relevant to computer science and related fields. Fellowships support promising PhD candidates of all backgrounds across Africa, Australia, Canada, East Asia, Europe, India, Latin America, the Middle East, New Zealand, Southeast Asia and the United States, with monetary awards paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution.
official.program_type: Industry-sponsored international doctoral fellowship awarded through university nomination
official.english_requirement: All application materials should be submitted in English.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply to this fellowship yourself - Google only accepts nominations submitted by universities during the application window, so the real task is persuading your department to nominate you, and internal deadlines at your university will precede Google's window. Since universities may nominate at most four students in Canada and the United States (three in most other regions), your competition is with your own labmates first. Award value varies enormously by region and stage - up to US $85K per year for two years in Canada and the United States, but as little as a one-year US $10K in East Asia - so read your region's terms before treating this as a funding centrepiece. The 2026 cycle closed on April 30, 2026 and the next window is unpublished, so set a reminder to check the program page in early spring.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD students in computer science or adjacent fields at accredited research universities in the listed regions, whose departments will nominate them and whose research aligns with Google's published research areas.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach your department or graduate school early about the internal nomination process and its internal cutoff
Align your proposal to one of Google's published research areas and the Google AI Principles

Prepare the components in advance: CV, transcripts, 2-3 recommendation letters (at least one from your thesis advisor), a research proposal of 3 pages maximum excluding references, and the advisor's one-page CV
For Canada, the United States, East Asia or Latin America, draft the 350-word essay responses on research impact and leadership
Ensure your department has the signed Department Chair cover sheet confirming eligibility
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply directly - Google rejects student-submitted applications outright
Missing your university's internal nomination cutoff, which runs before Google's window
Holding a comparable industry award, which disqualifies you (government or non-profit funding is exempt)
Falling below the region-specific stage rule, such as incomplete graduate coursework in Canada and the United States
Submitting a portfolio PDF instead of a single flat PDF, or exceeding the 3-page proposal limit
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Awards are paid to the university for distribution with no overhead assessed; coverage combinations differ by region (some cover stipend and travel only, others tuition and fees too), so uncovered costs depend on your region's terms.
document_audit: The Department Chair-signed cover sheet is mandatory for Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Canada, East Asia, the United States and Latin America
All materials must be in one flat PDF, with the proposal capped at 3 pages excluding references
Your primary PhD advisor needs a one-page CV as part of the package - request it well before the window
alerts: Recipients do not become Google employees, and the award does not improve your chances of a Google internship or job
You are not subject to intellectual property restrictions unless you complete a Google internship
You must remain enrolled full-time for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award, and past awardees cannot reapply
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: University-internal nomination first, then the university submits a single flat PDF through the portal during the application window (March 5 to April 30, 2026 for the last cycle); decisions follow by late August with public announcement by end of October.
